title: Reconcile compatibility delivery and issue closure in the guide
body:

Issue #9 closed after source merge `4f90164519167da3d7952d81a7a6211602ef28d5`, both independent final reviews, all six PR jobs and all six merged-main jobs. This reconciles the guide with those confirmed facts: retain #9 as a closed reference, remove it from remaining-work coverage/roadmap, update the compatibility row and refresh paginated backlog/history inputs. Local generation, five maintenance tests, browser/print and generated-output consistency pass. Coverage validation then identified the remaining #9 coverage entry, which was removed before successful generation. Existing architecture/viewer sources and receipts are unchanged. Every changed path is under `docs/work-guide/`. The same comparison and merged tree will be verified. No product code or specification changed.

title: Fix ordinary Codex current status across successive turns
body:
Ordinary Codex Desktop hooks report unknown ordering, so successive turns previously left activity unknown and kept the prior completion notice pending. The shared reducer now selects an eligible unseen turn start by receipt order, accepts its matching stop, and clears completion notices only for consumers configured to do so. Provider ordering stays unknown; an unseen delayed start can still select incorrectly.

Refs #137.

The change preserves independent attention and acknowledgment, bounds retired IDs to 256 with FIFO eviction, and recovers existing ambiguous version 1.0 stores without a reset. Agent-state 2.0.0 and Hub 0.2.0 mark the changed behavior while retaining lifecycle/snapshot/storage 1.0. The actual hook and pinned Pixoo/Nanoleaf consumers are exercised with disposable state and fake physical transports.

Validation: Node 24 build/type; 108 state tests and 68 Hub tests; both-language contracts/lifecycle/state consumers; isolated reproducible packages; MCP, setup, privacy/deadline, performance/isolation, workflow, dashboard/browser and real-consumer checks pass. A frozen pre-change export verifies recovery. The original ordinary lifecycle and parent-independence regressions were observed failing before their fixes. Workflow validates 11 specifications and 11 archived changes.

The guide inputs/output, state documentation and installed-update runbook are synchronized. Guide generation, five maintenance tests, browser/print and no-drift checks pass. Ownership diagrams retain their existing pins because the change stays inside the same reducer and adds no transport or writer.

Independent Standards and Specification review and all six current-head CI jobs are required before guarded merge. After merged-main checks, publish new immutable archives with checksums/source receipts, close #137, and reconcile confirmed delivery in a linked guide-only completion PR. Public guide publication, installation and the real Desktop/Pixoo retest remain separate; Pixoo #34 owns installed acceptance. Reset #138 and history #139 are excluded.

Delivery uses one coordinating writer and independent read-only reviewers. No live service, personal hook, database or physical device is changed.

title: Record 85HA keyboard and N30 mouse qualification findings
body:
The owner's packaging identifies an 8BitDo N Edition keyboard (85HA) and N30 mouse (85CA). The earlier R8 research lead does not describe this mouse. This candidate records the actual hardware, cited per-control/per-connection capabilities, Windows/Wispr/Codex interfaces, mapping ownership and a reversible operator trial.

Refs #64. This is the source-evidence candidate; #64 remains incomplete and #65 remains blocked. The keyboard's genuine held output, N30 event identities/selective suppression, installed app versions and a complete supported route are unqualified. No input observer, mapping write, microphone use, app dispatch or installation ran. Read-only Windows inventory failed because this session could not execute Windows tools.

The canonical desktop-control document and generated guide incorporate the new evidence. Guide inputs reconcile concurrent #63 closure and merged source history. Public guide publication remains separate.

Validation on the committed candidate:

- Node 24: `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` passed; 11 specifications, 10 archives and 15 workflow tests. This documentation introduces no behavior or wire-contract delta, so no new OpenSpec capability is needed.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`: all five tests passed.
- `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`: coverage, links, navigation, interactions and print restoration passed at six widths. Desktop/mobile/print renders were inspected. The guide covers 95 open issues, 130 linked issues, 52 roadmap nodes and nine diagrams.
- All nine Archify artifacts passed 9/9 deterministic checks; guide regeneration produced no drift. The standalone desktop-input viewer still fails its viewport check for vertical overflow, with identical dimensions and diagnostics to the previous artifact. This existing limitation is retained, not reported as a pass.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews, including Windows/input compatibility, and all six applicable hosted jobs are pending. Merge eligibility depends on their results and the missing qualification evidence; this PR has no automatic issue-closure keyword. Source work does not establish installed, application or physical acceptance.

title: Reconcile desktop-control documentation completion in the guide
body:
Refs #63. Completion follow-up to #140.

PR #140 delivered the desktop-control documentation as `0d1b0930efae23912b942f6e65560763402fe665`. Both independent reviews and all six PR plus six merged-main jobs passed; issue #63 is closed as completed. Guide issue #35 links the delivered document and marks that checklist item complete.

Record the remaining #63 completion details in the guide, label its documentation row complete, and start the desktop track at input qualification #64. Refresh the three backlogs and paginated repository histories. Preserve the independent shortcut path, downstream preset gates, and the concurrent #30 source/guide closeout from PRs #135/#142. No product, OpenSpec, architecture viewer or source-pin changes.

Validation at head `1ac4e2a14acdbcdc35b80ecb3a4a76d99629d764`, base/merge-base `10493718ee01dee78c290294f751829dd60ea91d`:

- Guide generation passed: 94 primary open issues, 12 guides, nine unchanged viewers, 52 roadmap nodes and 110 merged PRs.
- All five maintenance tests passed.
- Node 24.21.0 browser checks passed at six widths, including coverage, links, navigation, search, diagram inspection and print expansion/restoration. No page errors or main-page external requests.
- Postcommit regeneration produced no output drift; `git diff --check` passed. HTML SHA-256 `89b1436e29fd5803718cff61db2c52b67bc9be2920c45edd61b5b9bb9964d646`.

All eight changed paths are under `docs/work-guide/`. Both existing workflows exclude that directory for PR and main pushes. Current-head reads show zero runs/checks/statuses, consistent with the SDLC guide-only exception. The final scope/filter/protection and postmerge receipt remain required. Protection/ruleset reads return private-plan HTTP 403; no settings are changed. The guide UI exemption applies.

Independent Standards and Specification review round 3 both passed without findings on the comparison above. Rounds 1 and 2 passed without findings, but their final guards stopped when concurrent PRs #135 and #142 advanced main. Both revisions were merged into this branch, inputs reconciled and checks renewed; no force push or review correction was needed.

The coordinator owns the edits and delivery. The same two reviewers were requested at gpt-5.6-terra/high; three distinct agents used, no workers or advisor consultations, no promotions or effort changes. Actual runtime settings and usage are unexposed.

Public publication remains separate; the last verified public landing-page hash is `4d8f172a5025252c7b06551dfa862d1abe697fc532a54f75151d231217ed799e`. No installation, hardware/input, application, transport or visible-device acceptance is claimed.
